column5: Before his death, the converted king St Gwynllyw placed a protective curse on his sanctuary to punish any who dared desecrate or steal from it. When pirates later plundered the holy site, his vengeful spirit manifested to reclaim the sacred relics amidst a violent storm.

column3: The Haunting of Bumbler's Farm
column5: At the close of the 19th century, Bumbler's Farm in Shelfanger became plagued by violent poltergeist activity and the apparition of a spectral woman after a cursed candlestick was disturbed from a farm pond.

column3: The Curse of the Stockton Stone
column5: Moving a glacial megalith by the A146 in the 1930s supposedly triggered a fatal curse that brought sudden death to one of the workmen involved.

column3: The Cursed Cross of Langley
column5: Langley Cross was bound by a traditional curse warning that its removal from near the abbey would result in Langley Hall being destroyed by fire, a prophecy that partially fulfilled itself in 1801.

column3: The Witchcraft of Mrs Reeve
column5: In 1878, a farmyard worker in Lakes End believed he had been cursed with a sudden infestation of lice by a local woman reputed to be a witch. Upon threatening to retaliate against her, the affliction mysteriously vanished just as the woman learned of his words.

column3: The Cursed Goat's Head of Strumpshaw
column5: The haunted head of a goat left villagers in Strumpshaw trembling for decades.

column3: Father Ignatius on Elm Hill
column5: The twilight spirit of a curse-spreading holy man named Father Ignatius walks Norwich's Elm Hill carrying a large black Bible.

column3: The Green Lady of Costessey Hall
column5: Legend holds that the ruins of Costessey Hall are haunted by a benevolent Green Lady who guarded the historic estate and its secret Catholic heritage. According to local tradition, her spirit was bound to the hall's Thornbury Tower, casting a curse on anyone who attempted to fully demolish it.

column3: The Cursed Foundations of Horsham Priory
column5: When Norman knight Robert Fitzwalter attempted to build a monastery dedicated to St Faith at Kirkescrofte, mysterious forces repeatedly tore down by night what was constructed by day, forcing the abbey to be relocated to Horsham St Faith.

column3: The Cursed Foundations of Kirkescrofte
column5: Following a vow of gratitude to St. Faith, medieval nobles attempted to build a monastery at Kirkescrofte in Horsford, only for the masonry to collapse nightly until the project was relocated.

column3: The Cursed Cross of Gayton
column5: A wayside cross base in Gayton gained a sinister reputation after locals believed that every time the relic was moved, someone would die or be killed.

column3: The Cursed Goat's Head of Strumpshaw
column5: For decades, a mounted goat's head known as "Old Capricorn" hung in a Strumpshaw pub, drawing tales of poltergeist activity, sudden tragedies, and mysterious reappearances after being thrown into a river.

column3: The Prophecies and Curses of Corrag the Witch
column5: The witch Corrag issued warnings before the Glencoe Massacre and left behind a cursed sword and enduring local prophecies.

column3: The Vengeance of Tiddy Mun
column5: When Dutch engineers drained the Lincolnshire wetlands in the seventeenth century, the offended bog spirit Tiddy Mun inflicted a persistent curse of pestilence upon the local population. The plague of sickness and flooding only lifted after the villagers gathered at twilight to offer public apologies and appease the spirit.

column3: The White Lady of Czocha Castle
column5: After betraying her family to enemy forces in the 15th century, a woman named Gertrude was cursed by her brother to wander the halls of Czocha Castle for eternity, barred even from the gates of hell.

column3: The Cursed Chair of Thomas Busby
column5: A plain wooden chair in a North Yorkshire museum is said to bring sudden, untimely death to anyone who sits in it.

column3: The Cursed Stone of Dundrum
column5: An ancient standing stone in Dundrum carries a persistent curse that brings misfortune and disaster upon anyone who dares to touch, move, or disturb it. Believed to mark a protected druidic site, the stone's malignant aura punishes trespassers and vandals alike.

column3: The Cursed Butter Stone of Knockmany
column5: When giant Oonagh's hurried toss of a massive butter miscaun misses its target across the Tyrone valley, she places a fierce curse upon it, transforming the dairy lump into stone. Anyone who attempts to move or injure the boulder is doomed to suffer evil misfortune.

column3: The Curse of the Lambton Worm
column5: A young heir who skipped church to fish hooked a monstrous serpent, and when he later slew the beast without following a wise woman's instructions, he cursed nine generations of his family. True to the prophecy, for nearly ten generations the Lambtons met unnatural or unpeaceful ends.

column3: The Curse of the Wooden Man of Egeskov Castle
column5: Generations of owners have believed that moving a mysterious wooden doll resting in the attic rafters of a historic Danish castle will cause the entire building to sink into its moat on Christmas Eve. To keep the impending doom at bay, the family appeases the figure each year with a traditional bowl of rice pudding.

column3: The Boghall Brownie
column5: After being mistakenly offered warm blankets during a harsh winter, a loyal farm brownie curses the garments and abandons the homestead forever, leading to its permanent decline in prosperity.

column3: The Cursed Homing Stones of Seath Mòr
column5: The 14th-century grave of Clan Shaw chief Seath Mòr in Inverness-shire is topped with five protective stones carrying a lethal curse that strikes anyone who tampers with them or removes them from the tomb.

column3: The Curse of the Aspen Tree
column5: The aspen tree in Banffshire is believed to be cursed, causing its leaves to tremble constantly.

column3: The Curses of Devol Deviyo at Seenigama
column5: Devotees travel to a secluded offshore island shrine in Seenigama to invoke divine curses and retribution against adversaries by grinding chili peppers on stone slabs. Rooted in the folklore of the deity Devol Deviyo, this centuries-old practice serves as a ritualized channel for revenge and justice.

column3: The Curse of the Royal Tombs of Nan Madol
column5: When a foreign governor broke into the sealed ancient tombs of Nan Madol in defiance of local taboos, he was struck down by a deadly curse manifested in supernatural storms and sudden death. Local tradition warns that anyone who violates these sacred ruins will face divine retribution.

column3: The Curse of Ragnhild Tregagås
column5: In fourteenth-century Norway, a woman named Ragnhild Tregagås placed a malicious marital curse on her former lover and his new bride, invoking dark forces to induce impotence and tear the marriage apart.

column3: The Curse of Ämmänhauta
column5: According to local folklore in Vesilahti, a pact made with an 11th-century witch established a permanent curse upon anyone who passes her forest tomb without tossing a branch upon it. Passing travelers and villagers have faithfully adhered to this ritual across generations to avoid invoking her wrath.

column3: Surech and Dulei
column5: Two young lovers from rival Palauan villages defied the bitter social enmity between their clans, which they considered a curse, and chose to leap into the sea together rather than be separated.

column3: The Enchanted Maiden of Salto del Pilón
column5: An enigmatic water maiden guards a sacred waterfall and deep pool in Panama, enchanting treasure-seekers and testing their greed before luring them into the abyss. Those who fail her tests or succumb to her waters vanish into the legend forever.

column3: The Curse of the Ass-Head
column5: Following their forced displacement by British settlers, indigenous Koya Temne leaders performed a nocturnal ceremony burying an ass head to curse the land of Freetown. This hex was believed to ensure that the territory would remain politically fractured and unsettled until historical injustices were resolved.

column3: The Phantoms of Castillo La Alboraya
column5: Passing down generations through the local community, a sinister curse and haunting atmosphere cling to an abandoned colonial fortress in Barranquilla where dark deeds once took place. Locals tell of ghostly apparitions and a phantom black stallion whose midnight gallop terrorizes those who stay too late near the grounds.
